model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for several language model variants. The x-axis represents "#Iteration" on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 140,000, with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents "Loss" on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1.

Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different model configuration. The purple line labeled "Vanilla" starts at approximately 3.4 at iteration 0 and decreases steeply in the early iterations, then gradually levels off, reaching approximately 2.50 by iteration 140,000. The blue line labeled "StrmLLM (n=64)" also starts near 3.4 and follows a similar steep initial decline but plateaus at a notably higher loss, ending at approximately 2.62 by iteration 140,000. The orange line labeled "SepLLM (n=64)" starts near 3.4 and decreases to approximately 2.52 by iteration 140,000, closely tracking the Vanilla line but remaining slightly above it. The green line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H)" follows a very similar trajectory to the orange line, ending at approximately 2.52–2.53. The red line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" also follows a similar path, ending at approximately 2.51–2.52 by iteration 140,000. The dark blue line labeled "SepLLM (n=128)" starts near 3.4 and decreases to approximately 2.53 by iteration 140,000, following a trajectory close to the other SepLLM variants. All lines exhibit shaded regions around them indicating variability or confidence bounds. The StrmLLM (n=64) line is distinctly separated above the cluster of Vanilla and SepLLM variants throughout most of the training, while the Vanilla, SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128) lines remain closely grouped together in the lower portion of the plot.
